## Summary

The workflow (`anndata.experimental.concat_on_disk`) concatenates multiple on-disk `.h5ad` study shards with `join="outer"`. When the outer join introduces new features, the alt-axis mappings (`varm`, `obsm`) must be reindexed. In this `anndata` snapshot, `Reindexer` in `source/src/anndata/_core/merge.py` did not handle the on-disk element types it actually encounters, causing the failure users reported.

I fixed **two bugs**, both in `source/src/anndata/_core/merge.py` (the only file changed):

1. **Sparse on-disk datasets were routed to the dense reindex path.** `Reindexer.apply` had no case for `BaseCompressedSparseDataset` (e.g. `varm/sparse_embedding`), so it fell through to `_apply_to_array`, which cannot reindex a sparse matrix. It now dispatches these to `_apply_to_sparse` via `el.to_memory()`, so the existing sparse logic applies (correctly 0-filling absent rows).

2. **Dense reindex passed a raw `h5py.Dataset` to `pd.api.extensions.take`.** That API requires a NumPy/extension array (it calls `arr.take`), and `h5py.Dataset` only implements the array protocol — hence `AttributeError: 'Dataset' object has no attribute 'take'`. `_apply_to_array` now materializes non-`ndarray` inputs with `np.asarray` before calling `take`, which is bounded by the element's own size and stays practical on large studies.
